::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Can a region of the $xy$ plane be infinite in area and topologically closed?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2316186/can-a-region-of-the-xy-plane-be-infinite-in-area-and-topologically-closed), asked by [Michael Stachowsky](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/337044/michael-stachowsky) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-06-09; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Is it possible to create a region in the $xy$ plane that has infinite area but contains all of its boundary points?  In other words, if I am introducing a theorem that begins: "Let R be a closed region in the $xy$ plane", do I need to also specify that R is finite?
:::

What about the region
$$D = \left\{(x,y)\mid x \geq 1, 0 \leq y \leq 1/x\right\}$$
A few more examples came to mind, but then I wasn't sure on the definition of region.
